messages:
rachael: quick follow-up from today — capturing the hiring/structure Qs so managers have a single place to check.
emma: thanks. first: what does a clean handoff look like? managers asking for a checklist they can use tonight.
lina: Manager Handoff checklist incoming. Core items: written ownership doc, 10-business-day overlap where feasible, updated on-call rota, backlog triage notes, and customer comms template.
jorge: can we get a tiny ownership doc template? makes it easier to be consistent.
ops-bot: doc-publish: "people-ops/ownership-handoff-template.md" at 2465123400
jorge: perfect. next — hiring freeze scope: is it org-wide or scoped to teams?
rachael: scoped. freeze applies to non-priority buckets; priority = infra, enterprise ops, customer SLAs. People Ops will tag reqs in Greenhouse as "priority" or "freeze".
matt: finance guidance: when headcount shifts, filing a reallocation in the finance portal starts the 3-business-day fast-track. tag requests with "headcount-transfer-priority" to expedite.
renee: for offers in flight: do we pause pending offers or continue outreach?
lina: continue for accepted offers and for priority roles. For non-priority offers mid-process, recruiters should pause onsite scheduling and notify candidates with the standard pause template. template in People Ops doc.
emma: promotions? people are worried transfers will block promotions mid-cycle.
rachael: promotions continue. if a promotion interview/panel conflicts with transfer windows, People Ops will coordinate to preserve timelines. transfers don't restart time-in-role requirements.
jorge: visa/relocation edge case: moving someone cross-country within Redwood — extra approvals?
lina: any transfer affecting visa sponsorship requires Legal + People Ops approval and should be flagged early. expect extra lead time; do not assume immediate transfer.
renee: tactical ask: can teams request temporary dotted-line assignments instead of permanent moves? keeps continuity.
rachael: yes — dotted-line 30-60 day assignments encouraged. track them in the team-roster doc so payroll & PD coverage are accurate.
ops-bot: note: "people-ops/req-tagging-policy.md" published at 2465123405
jorge: on-call swaps — do we expect teams to update PagerDuty before effective date?
rachael: yes. update PD, set explicit escalation ownership, and run a 2-day overlap for critical services. infra teams: please run smoke tests post-handoff.
emma: will there be a public readout after each wave? managers want metrics to understand impact.
rachael: short readout after each wave: moved headcount, offers affected, number of contracts fast-tracked, and customer incidents (if any). planned within 4 business days of wave close.
lina: also publishing manager talking points + an FAQ for ICs today — will include where to send exceptions and a short decision matrix.
matt: minor budget Q: who approves reallocation to a different product line? finance signs off after the manager files the reallocation form; People Ops validates headcount policy.
jorge: how strict is the 10-day overlap? some hires can't overlap due to schedules.
rachael: aim for 10 business days, but exceptions allowed if there's a documented plan and exec sign-off for high-risk transitions.
emma: small request: can we have a single channel for transfer exceptions so People Ops doesn't get DM spam?
lina: yes, creating #people-ops-transfers now. use that + the exception form.
ops-bot: channel-created: #people-ops-transfers at 2465123410
rachael: thanks all. posting links here when docs are up and running. manager-only sync tomorrow 3pm PT for Qs. :white_check_mark:
__notes: All-hands follow-up: manager handoff checklist, freeze scope, Greenhouse tagging, finance reallocation SLA, offers in flight, promotions preserved, visas, dotted-line assignments, PD updates, wave readouts, and a single exceptions channel. Short Slack-style messages.
